clue.text: Sleepy youngster we hear did sound that horn?

definitions.text: Sleepy youngster we hear did sound that horn?

parts.words: Sleepy youngster we hear did sound that horn?
parts.note: the nursery-rhyme child told to blow his horn, who is found asleep under the haystack; the last word of his name sounds like the past tense of blow, so a small lad who blew that horn

explanation.surface: A drowsy child is suspected of having been the one who tooted that horn.
explanation.walkthrough: The nursery rhyme begins 'come blow your horn' and ends with the boy fast asleep under the haystack; his colour name sounds like 'blew', so the name itself says a little boy did sound the horn.
explanation.definitionFit: The rhyme's horn-blowing shepherd boy is famously asleep under a haystack, hence a sleepy youngster.

clue.text: Uncle married out of season, on the rebound

indicators.note: something on the rebound bounces back, so the shortened season is read in the opposite direction
the married abbreviation is taken out of the season, leaving it one letter short

parts.note: summer is a season

explanation.surface: A married uncle is getting over a break-up out of season.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of' removes one M from SUMMER to leave SUMER, and 'on the rebound' turns that round.
explanation.definitionFit: Uncle Remus is the storyteller of Joel Chandler Harris's folk tales, so the name fits the title.

clue.text: Servant, sadly mistreated, forced to have a hearing

indicators.note: mistreated suggests handled roughly, so the letters of sadly are knocked into a new order
a hearing is something listened to, so the word for forced is taken by ear rather than by spelling

parts.note: made, as in made to do something, means forced

explanation.surface: A servant, sadly ill-treated, is made to face a tribunal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mistreated' rearranges SADLY into LADYS; 'to have a hearing' turns MADE into its sound-alike MAID.
explanation.definitionFit: A lady's maid is a female domestic who attends her mistress personally, a kind of servant.

clue.text: Being painful, almost, to eat and swallow

indicators.note: eating takes something inside, so the shortened word for being painful takes in the conjunction
almost means not quite all, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: smarting means being painful, as a sting is
taken as written

explanation.surface: Something hurts, almost too much to eat and swallow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swallow' looks like a verb next to 'eat'; it is the bird, and 'Being painful' is one piece, not a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The sand martin is a small brown bird of the swallow family that nests in sandy banks.

clue.text: What may break a girl

definitions.meaning: daybreak: first light is said to break each morning
a girl's name, as in the singer Ms French

explanation.definitionFit: The first light of day is said to break, and the same word is a common female first name.

clue.text: Monopolies, a certain number, secured by mild strikes

indicators.note: something secured by another is held within it, so the number sits inside the gentle blows

parts.note: pats are gentle taps, mild strikes
ten is a particular number

explanation.surface: Industries with monopolies have suffered only a handful of half-hearted walkouts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strikes' suggests industrial action; here the strikes are light blows, PATS, holding TEN.
explanation.definitionFit: A patent grants an inventor exclusive rights to an invention, a legal monopoly for a set period.

clue.text: At home, I put nameless dog on lead — he kept escaping

indicators.note: a piece put on lead goes in front, so the shortened dog comes before the rest
the abbreviation N for name is removed from the word for dog

parts.note: a hound is a hunting dog
in means at home

explanation.surface: Back home, I clip the lead on to an unnamed dog that keeps running away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nameless' drops N from HOUND to leave HOUD, and 'on lead' puts it first, ahead of IN and I.
explanation.definitionFit: Harry Houdini was the famous escapologist, freeing himself from chains, locks and tanks.

clue.text: Right chuffed to be one of the family

parts.note: chuffed is British slang for pleased, elated

explanation.surface: Someone is really pleased to be welcomed into the family.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Right' reads as an intensifier, as in 'right pleased', but gives R. 'Chuffed' is British slang for delighted.
explanation.definitionFit: Being related means being kin, connected by blood or marriage to the rest of a family.

clue.text: Building over frozen soil, diverting river to the west

indicators.note: diverting sends something along a different course, so one letter is shifted from its place
in an across clue west is the left-hand end, so the shifted letter goes to the front

parts.note: O is the cricket abbreviation for over
tundra is the frozen treeless ground of the Arctic

explanation.surface: Engineers are putting up a building on permafrost and rerouting a river westwards.
explanation.walkthrough: O plus TUNDRA gives OTUNDRA; 'diverting' and 'to the west' move its R to the front.
explanation.definitionFit: A rotunda is a round building, usually topped with a dome.

clue.text: An objection about a member of the band

indicators.note: about can mean turned round, so the objection is written backwards

parts.note: but, as in no ifs or buts, is an objection

explanation.surface: Someone raises an objection about one of the musicians in the group.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns the whole of A BUT round, so the objection ends up in front.
explanation.definitionFit: The tuba is the large low brass instrument found in a brass or military band.

clue.text: Camp leader's brief pause, slowly coming to premature end

indicators.note: brief means cut short, so the punctuation pause loses its final letter

parts.note: a comma marks a pause in a sentence

indicators.note: something ending prematurely stops short, so the final letter of the tempo marking is lost

parts.note: andante is the musical direction for a moderately slow pace

explanation.surface: The camp commander's short break is gradually drawing to an early close.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brief' trims COMMA to COMM; 'slowly' is the musical term ANDANTE, and 'coming to premature end' trims it to ANDANT.
explanation.definitionFit: A commandant is the officer in charge of a military establishment such as a prison camp.

clue.text: Making up elegy, first off suppressing accent

indicators.note: suppressing holds something down and in, so the shortened elegy encloses the accent
the first letter is taken off the poem of mourning

parts.note: a lament is a mournful poem, an elegy
tone, a manner of voice, can mean accent

explanation.surface: Someone is composing a mournful poem, first of all toning down an accent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Making up' suggests composing or inventing; it means reconciling, making amends.
explanation.definitionFit: Atonement is making amends for a wrong, as in making up for a fault.

clue.text: One grazing bone — it's broken into two bits

indicators.note: a thing broken into has something forced inside it, so the bone goes between the two digits

parts.note: binary digits, or bits, are 0 and 1, read as the letters O and I
a rib is a bone

explanation.surface: A grazing animal's bone has snapped into two pieces.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bits' are binary digits, 0 and 1, which look like the letters O and I; RIB goes between them.
explanation.definitionFit: The oribi is a small African antelope that feeds on grass, so it is a grazer.

clue.text: As mammals, he or she so cryptically represented?

definitions.text: As mammals, he or she so cryptically represented?

indicators.note: cryptically represented says the letters of he or she so are shown in disguise, rearranged

parts.note: read the answer's first word as letters to scramble and its second word as the signal (bats means crazy), and the rearranged letters spell he or she so
bats are flying mammals

explanation.surface: A riddle asks how mammals might be shown as he or she in some coded form.
explanation.walkthrough: The scrambled letters of HE OR SHE SO come first, then BATS; and since 'bats' is itself a common anagram signal, the whole name reads as an instruction to scramble that phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: These are insect-eating bats with a horseshoe-shaped nose leaf, and bats are mammals.

clue.text: The bench of sporting HQ with "Swing Low," for example

parts.note: Lord's, the London cricket ground, is the headquarters of cricket
Swing Low, Sweet Chariot is an African-American spiritual

explanation.surface: The magistrates of a sports headquarters are paired with a famous rugby anthem.
explanation.walkthrough: Lord's is the London cricket ground known as the home of cricket; 'Swing Low' is sung by English rugby crowds, which pulls towards sport.
explanation.definitionFit: The bishops who sit in the House of Lords occupy the bishops' bench there, so the term names that bench.

clue.text: Athenian is second to get canned

indicators.note: the second is made to get the can around it, so the short time goes inside the container

parts.note: to can something is to put it in a tin
mo, as in half a mo, is a moment or second

explanation.surface: A man from Athens is the second person to be sacked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'canned' looks like 'fired'; here MO, a second, is put in TIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's Timon of Athens is the title character, a citizen of that city.

clue.text: Survive a short time, becoming late

parts.note: to last is to survive or endure
a minute is a short time

explanation.surface: Someone holds on briefly before turning up late.
explanation.definitionFit: Something done at the eleventh hour, just before a deadline, is described as coming very late.

clue.text: Area with rubles for change?

indicators.note: change means an alteration, so the letters of area-abbreviation plus rubles are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A traveller asks whether this region gives roubles as change.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition too: the country is an area that uses rubles, and change also means the coins handed back.
explanation.definitionFit: The country's currency is the Belarusian ruble, so it is an area where rubles serve as change.

clue.text: Work in home, turning up at meal — tongue

indicators.note: in a down clue turning up reads the letters from the bottom upward, so the abbreviation is reversed

parts.note: DIY, do-it-yourself, is work done in the home
a dish is a course or meal

explanation.surface: Someone does a job at home and then arrives at a meal to eat tongue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tongue' looks like food after 'meal'; it means language.
explanation.definitionFit: Yiddish is a language, and tongue is a standard synonym for language.

clue.text: In luck, succeeded? On the contrary

definitions.text: In luck, succeeded? On the contrary

indicators.note: in as written would put one piece inside the other
the instruction is turned around, so the succeeded abbreviation goes inside luck rather than the other way

parts.note: lot, as in one's lot in life, means fortune or luck
S is the abbreviation for succeeded, as in family trees

explanation.surface: Someone asks if they were lucky and succeeded, only to be told the opposite.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as wordplay, 'In luck, succeeded' puts LOT inside S; 'On the contrary' flips that to S in LOT. As a whole, the clue's opposite of succeeding is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Failing to win or succeed is the reverse of success, so having been beaten is the contrary.

clue.text: Proceeding to have strong feeling, getting two articles for nothing

indicators.note: for means in place of, so the two articles replace the zero-shaped letter

parts.note: emotion is strong feeling
O looks like zero, nothing
an and a are the two indefinite articles

explanation.surface: Someone acting on deep feeling gets a couple of items for free.
explanation.walkthrough: 'articles' suggests goods; here they are grammar's AN and A, which take the place of the first O in EMOTION.
explanation.definitionFit: An emanation is something that issues or proceeds from a source, as light from a lamp.

clue.text: Shakespeare's plot device all the same succeeds after time

indicators.note: after places the word for succeeds behind the abbreviation for time

parts.note: identical means all the same
wins means succeeds

explanation.surface: Shakespeare's plotting nevertheless pays off in the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'all the same' reads as 'nevertheless' but means IDENTICAL. Shakespeare's Comedy of Errors and Twelfth Night turn on twins mistaken for each other.
explanation.definitionFit: Mix-ups between look-alike siblings drive The Comedy of Errors, so such pairs are a classic plot device of his.

clue.text: As one goes by, grab a carnation, typically

definitions.meaning: to accost or detain someone passing so as to talk to them at length
a flower worn in the lapel slit, a carnation being the usual choice

explanation.surface: Snatch a carnation from a flower stall while walking past.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to waylay someone to talk to; the noun is a flower worn in a lapel, often a carnation.

clue.text: Place to pay where old lawyer breaks into what may be wisdom

indicators.note: breaking into somewhere means getting inside it, so the old lawyer goes inside the wisdom item

parts.note: a wisdom tooth is one kind of tooth
LLB, Bachelor of Laws, is a law degree held by a lawyer

explanation.surface: Somewhere you pay a fee is where a former solicitor burgles a sage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wisdom' looks abstract; it is a wisdom tooth. The old lawyer goes in after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A booth at a bridge or motorway where drivers hand over a charge is a place to pay.

clue.text: Wrong code is used by English administrative area

indicators.note: used by places the English abbreviation next to the rearranged letters, at the end
wrong means faulty, so the letters of code and is are put in a different order

explanation.surface: A badly written code is being used by an English local authority.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wrong' rearranges CODE and IS into DIOCES, followed by E.
explanation.definitionFit: A diocese is the district under a bishop's authority, an area of church administration.

clue.text: Heave, suppressing outward signs of malaria, in new bout

indicators.note: suppressing holds something in, so the heave contains the letters taken from malaria

parts.note: to retch is to heave, as with nausea

indicators.note: the outward signs are the outermost letters, first and last, of malaria

explanation.surface: A malaria patient tries not to vomit, though the symptoms return in a fresh attack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outward signs of malaria' looks like symptoms; it is M and A, the outer letters, inside RETCH.
explanation.definitionFit: A rematch is a second contest between the same opponents, a fresh bout.

clue.text: Inner personality of a parent from Belfast?

indicators.note: from is taken to place the parent after the Belfast abbreviation

parts.note: Belfast is the capital of Northern Ireland, abbreviated NI
ma is mother, a parent

explanation.surface: A question about the inner self of a mother or father from Belfast.
explanation.walkthrough: NI stands for Northern Ireland, signalled by its capital Belfast.
explanation.definitionFit: In Jungian psychology this is the inner self or soul, the true personality behind the persona.

clue.text: Feature of river that's endlessly strange

indicators.note: endlessly means without its end, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: weird means strange

explanation.surface: Something on a river is oddly without end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' drops the last letter of WEIRD.
explanation.definitionFit: A weir is a low dam across a river, a common feature of one.
